questions.stem: A shipper consigns electronics to a trusted repeat buyer and wants the receiver to collect without presenting any original transport document. Which instrument achieves this while remaining legally non-negotiable?
options: Negotiable Bill of Lading
Sea Waybill
To-Order Bill of Lading
Straight Bill of Lading endorsed in blank
questions.why: A sea waybill is non-negotiable — the named consignee collects on identity proof alone; no original document needs to be surrendered or couriered.
questions.deepDive: The sea waybill (SWB) and bill of lading (B/L) serve fundamentally different commercial purposes. A B/L is a document of title — whoever holds the original controls the cargo; this is essential for letter-of-credit trade where a bank needs a security interest over goods in transit. A sea waybill is merely a receipt and evidence of contract; the named consignee simply proves identity to collect — no original required. This makes SWBs faster, cheaper, and ideal for intra-company shipments or established trading relationships. The trade-off: SWBs cannot be traded or pledged to banks as collateral, making them unsuitable where a bank needs a lien over cargo. Electronic bills of lading (BOLERO, WAVE, essDOCS) now bridge this gap, offering negotiability without paper logistics — an area regulators are actively standardising globally.

questions.stem: A Bangladesh exporter ships woven fabric pre-cut into shirt shapes but not yet sewn. Under the WCO Harmonized System, which General Rule of Interpretation (GRI) determines that customs should classify these cut panels as shirts rather than fabric?
options: GRI 1 — heading wording controls; classify as woven fabric
GRI 2(a) — incomplete-article rule; classify under finished shirt if essential character is present
GRI 3(b) — essential character of a mixture or composite good
GRI 6 — subheading-level classification takes precedence
questions.why: GRI 2(a) extends a tariff heading to incomplete or unfinished articles if they already present the essential character of the complete article — so pre-cut shirt panels classify under HS 62, not HS 54 fabric.
questions.deepDive: The Harmonized System (HS) is a 6-digit global tariff classification framework maintained by the WCO covering ~98% of world trade. Its six General Rules of Interpretation are applied sequentially. GRI 2(a) — the 'incomplete article' rule — is pivotal across global manufacturing: it extends headings to cover incomplete articles if they present the essential character of the finished good (a car body without an engine is still HS 8703). In Bangladesh's RMG sector this distinction is commercially critical: fabric (HS 54/55) and cut components (HS 61/62) attract different GSP tariff rates in the EU and UK — sometimes the difference between 0% and 12%. Post-LDC graduation, Bangladesh loses preference margins that currently shelter this classification advantage, making correct HS classification a major cost variable.

questions.stem: After the Panama Canal's expanded locks opened in 2016, which vessel class — capable of transiting the new locks — drove billions in US East Coast port infrastructure investment at Savannah, Baltimore, and New York?
options: VLCC (Very Large Crude Carrier)
Original Panamax (~4,500 TEU)
Neo-Panamax / New Panamax (~13,000–14,500 TEU)
ULCV (Ultra-Large Container Vessel, 18,000+ TEU)
questions.why: Neo-Panamax vessels (up to ~366m LOA, 49m beam, 15.2m draft) fit the new locks; US East Coast ports spent billions deepening channels to receive them, fundamentally restructuring the Transpacific trade routing.
questions.deepDive: Container vessel classes are defined by the physical constraints they must pass through. Original Panamax (≤4,500 TEU): 294m long, 32.3m beam, 12m draft — sized for the old Canal locks. The 2016 expansion created Neo-Panamax: up to 366m, 49m beam, 15.2m draft, ~13,000–14,500 TEU. This triggered massive US East Coast dredging programmes (Savannah Harbor Expansion, NY/NJ channel deepening). ULCVs (18,000–24,000+ TEU) are too large even for the new locks — they operate exclusively on Asia–Europe via Suez. The vessel class choice is central to liner network design: ULCVs minimise per-unit cost but require very few, very large gateway ports. For Bangladesh, Neo-Panamax feeder connections to Colombo or Port Klang determine the frequency and cost of Chittagong's access to mainlane trade.

questions.stem: Bangladesh maritime authorities board a foreign-flagged vessel at Chittagong, inspect SOLAS certificates, MARPOL compliance, and MLC 2006 crew conditions — then detain it for deficiencies. This authority derives from which international regime?
options: Flag State Control — the ship's flag nation enforces standards globally
Port State Control (PSC) — coastal states inspect foreign vessels in their ports
Classification Society Survey — the vessel's class society inspects for structural safety
Charterer's Pre-Fixture Inspection — commercial vetting by the cargo owner
questions.why: Port State Control gives coastal states authority under SOLAS, MARPOL, and MLC to inspect any foreign-flagged vessel in their ports and detain sub-standard ships until deficiencies are corrected.
questions.deepDive: Port State Control (PSC) is the system by which a coastal nation inspects foreign-flagged vessels visiting its ports for compliance with SOLAS (Safety of Life at Sea), MARPOL (marine pollution), MLC 2006 (seafarer labour), and STCW (crew training). Authority derives from the law of the sea: once inside a port, the coastal state has jurisdiction regardless of the vessel's flag. Nine regional PSC MOUs (Paris, Tokyo, Indian Ocean, etc.) coordinate globally, sharing detention records to prevent 'port shopping.' Bangladesh falls under the Indian Ocean MOU. A detained vessel cannot depart until deficiencies are corrected — daily charter-rate exposure of $10,000–30,000 for a container ship. Panama, Comoros, and Palau flags historically attract higher PSC detention rates than Norway or Germany, driving 'flag discrimination' in commercial chartering.

questions.stem: After the 2M partnership (Maersk + MSC) dissolved in early 2025, Maersk formed a new operational alliance. What is it called, and who is its partner carrier?
options: THE Alliance — Maersk + Hapag-Lloyd + ONE
Gemini Cooperation — Maersk + Hapag-Lloyd
Premier Alliance — Maersk + CMA CGM
Ocean Alliance — Maersk + COSCO + Evergreen
questions.why: The Gemini Cooperation — Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, launched February 1, 2025 — replaced 2M with a hub-and-spoke model explicitly targeting 90%+ schedule reliability.
questions.deepDive: The container shipping alliance landscape restructured dramatically in 2025. MSC — now the world's largest carrier — went fully independent after 2M broke up, giving it maximum pricing flexibility unconstrained by slot obligations. Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd formed the Gemini Cooperation (launched February 1, 2025), targeting a stated 90%+ schedule reliability vs. the industry average ~55%. Gemini operates a hub-and-spoke model with fewer, larger mainlane vessels connecting to secondary ports via feeder services — departing from traditional point-to-point port pairing. THE Alliance remnants (ONE, Yang Ming, HMM) rebranded as the Premier Alliance; Ocean Alliance (CMA CGM, COSCO, Evergreen, OOCL) continues unchanged. Commercial implication for Bangladesh: feeder access from Chittagong to Gemini mainlane hubs (e.g. Colombo, Port Klang) is now negotiated outside the old alliance framework, potentially changing frequency and pricing.

questions.stem: Lord Curzon's 1905 partition of Bengal was reversed in 1911 under mass nationalist pressure. What was the most consequential political outcome of the reversal for the subcontinent's long-run trajectory?
options: It permanently reconciled Hindu and Muslim political leadership within the Indian National Congress

It reinforced Muslim separatism — Muslim League leaders read the reversal as proof that Congress-led Hindu agitation could override Muslim interests, accelerating the case for a separate Muslim political vehicle
It discredited the Swadeshi movement, which collapsed immediately following the British concession
It triggered the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1911, which granted Muslims separate electorates for the first time
questions.why: The reversal was widely interpreted by Muslim League leaders as Congress mass mobilisation overriding a settlement favourable to East Bengal Muslims — strengthening the argument for separate political representation.
questions.deepDive: Curzon's October 16, 1905 partition of Bengal created a Muslim-majority East Bengal & Assam and a Hindu-majority West Bengal. The backlash produced the Swadeshi movement — boycott of British goods, mass cloth-burning — and split Congress between Moderates and Extremists (the 'Lal Bal Pal' trio: Tilak, Pal, Lajpat Rai, demanding swaraj). When Britain reversed the partition in 1911, Muslim elites in Dhaka concluded their interests could be overridden by sustained Hindu agitation — sharpening the argument for a separate political vehicle. The Muslim League (founded in Dhaka, 1906) grew more assertive. The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909, not 1911) had already institutionalised separate Muslim electorates. Together — partition, reversal, separate electorates — these events form the direct genealogy of the 1947 partition and Bangladesh's 1971 independence. The 1905 partition literally drew the map of what later became East Pakistan and then Bangladesh.

questions.stem: The Strait of Malacca narrows to approximately 2.7 km at the Phillips Channel near Singapore. Roughly what share of global seaborne trade by value passes through it each year?
questions.why: ~80,000–90,000 vessels transit Malacca annually, carrying roughly 20–25% of global trade by value — including ~80% of China's seaborne oil imports — making it the world's busiest maritime chokepoint by vessel count.
questions.deepDive: The Strait of Malacca — 800 km long between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra — narrows to 2.7 km at the Phillips Channel, with a minimum navigable depth of ~25 metres that limits laden VLCCs. Roughly 80,000–90,000 vessels transit annually, carrying ~25% of global trade and about a third of global container traffic, plus vast quantities of Gulf crude heading to China, Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan. China's 'Malacca Dilemma' — over-reliance on a chokepoint flanked by Singapore (a close US partner) — has driven the China-Myanmar Economic Corridor pipeline, the Kyaukphyu deepwater port, and BRI land-bridge ambitions. A closure would reroute ships via Lombok or Sunda Straits, adding 2–4 transit days and hundreds of dollars per TEU. For MGH's Bangladesh operations, Malacca's health is existential: most Chittagong export containers route through or near it en route to East Asia and the US West Coast.

questions.stem: Bangladesh's nominal GDP just crossed $500 billion; the IMF's PPP-adjusted figure is roughly 3× larger (~$1.5–1.8T). What specific economic phenomenon does the PPP adjustment correct for?
options: The informal economy not captured in official national accounts
Differences in domestic price levels — a dollar buys far more goods and services in Bangladesh than in the US
Currency speculation and black-market exchange rate premiums over the official BDT rate
Seasonal inflation spikes in food and fuel not smoothed in GDP deflators
questions.why: PPP adjusts for the fact that a dollar buys far more in Bangladesh than in the US — correcting for price-level differences so that real productive capacity and living standards are not understated by nominal exchange rates.
questions.deepDive: Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) is the hypothetical exchange rate at which two currencies would buy an identical basket of goods. Formalised by the IMF/World Bank International Comparison Program and popularised by The Economist's Big Mac Index (1986), PPP corrects a systematic bias in nominal GDP comparisons: developing-country currencies appear 'weak' partly because non-tradeable goods (haircuts, housing, meals) are cheap locally. A Bangladeshi earning BDT 50,000/month has far more real purchasing power than the ~$460 nominal USD equivalent implies. PPP-adjusted GDP ~$1.5–1.8T puts Bangladesh inside the global top 30 — largely invisible in nominal rankings. This matters strategically for MNC cost models, IMF lending capacity calculations, and development economics. But nominal GDP governs hard realities: dollar-denominated debt servicing, import capacity, and hard-currency export earnings — making Bangladesh Bank's FX management and the current account balance so consequential for businesses with cross-border treasury exposure.

questions.stem: UNESCO's International Mother Language Day — observed every February 21 — was established to honour the 1952 Language Movement martyrs. What specific policy were students protesting when police shot them at Dhaka University?
options: The British colonial ban on teaching Bengali at Dhaka University post-Partition
Pakistan's declaration that Urdu alone would be the national language, excluding Bangla despite it being spoken by the majority of Pakistan's total population
The exclusion of Bangla from the United Nations' list of official languages in 1948
India's imposition of Hindi as the medium of instruction in East Bengal schools
questions.why: Pakistan's 1948 Urdu-only national language declaration was rejected by East Pakistan's Bangla-speaking majority — protests on February 21, 1952 ended when police killed students at Dhaka University.
questions.deepDive: The 1952 Language Movement — Bhasha Andolan — is one of history's most consequential linguistic protests and the foundational act of Bangladeshi national consciousness. Pakistan's founder Jinnah declared Urdu the sole national language in 1948, despite East Pakistan's ~55% share of total Pakistani population being Bangla-speaking. Resistance built until February 21, 1952, when police opened fire on Dhaka University demonstrators, killing Abul Barkat, Rafiquddin Ahmed, and others — the Bhasha Shahids. The Shaheed Minar monument was built in their honour. UNESCO declared February 21 International Mother Language Day in November 1999, effective from 2000, globalising the date as a celebration of linguistic diversity. The Language Movement is the first distinct act of the independence struggle: it established that Bengali identity was incompatible with Pakistani statehood, setting the trajectory to the 1971 Liberation War. Bangla is the 7th most spoken language globally by native speakers, at ~230 million — and the only language for which people died in a national sovereignty struggle.

questions.stem: Regulators worldwide designate sub-6GHz spectrum (especially 3.5GHz C-band) as the primary band for broad national 5G NR coverage rather than millimeter wave (mmWave, 24–86GHz). What is the core physical reason mmWave cannot serve as a national coverage layer?
options: mmWave signals carry less data per hertz than sub-6GHz signals
mmWave signals attenuate rapidly over distance and are blocked by walls, rain, and foliage — limiting cell coverage radius to roughly 100–300 metres
The ITU reserves the mmWave band exclusively for satellite and radar applications
mmWave base stations require substantially more power per transmitted bit at scale
questions.why: Higher frequency = shorter wavelength = much faster path-loss and poor obstacle penetration; mmWave cells cover ~100–300 m vs. several kilometres for sub-6GHz, making national rollout economically impractical.
questions.deepDive: Radio frequency propagation follows a fundamental physics trade-off: lower frequency (longer wavelength) → greater range and obstacle penetration, lower peak bandwidth capacity per channel. Sub-6GHz (especially 3.5 GHz C-band) balances range and capacity — a single base station covers kilometres, penetrates building walls, and handles thousands of simultaneous devices. Millimeter wave (mmWave, 24–86 GHz) offers extraordinary bandwidth — multi-gigabit speeds — but signals attenuate severely in rain, are blocked by walls, foliage, and even humidity, and realistically cover only 100–300 metres per small cell. mmWave therefore concentrates in dense, controlled venues: stadiums, airports, convention centres, factory floors. Spectrum auction economics reflect this scarcity differential: sub-6GHz bands sell for enormous premiums. Bangladesh Telecom Regulatory Commission's spectrum allocation decisions directly affect whether BD carriers can build cost-effective 5G for port logistics digitalisation, warehouse automation, and supply-chain IoT — areas directly relevant to logistics operators like MGH.
